newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares end down but off lows, Telecom regains.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares end down but off lows, Telecom regains.

text.p: * New Zealand share prices end lower on high turnover
* Telecom partly regains lost ground
* No respite seen as reporting season progresses
Price movements at close

New Zealand share prices ended weaker but off their lows on Thursday, following the extreme volatility in leading stock Telecom.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index closed 15.96 points down at 2,274.19 on high turnover of NZ$100 million, Telecom accounting for $72.48 million of the total.
The index had fallen to 2,258.41 when Telecom slumped to NZ$6.29 earlier in session, following a sharply weaker close in New York where its ADRs are listed.
Wall Street stocks had fallen 55.03 points to close at 6,983.18 after cautionary comments from Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan sent shivers through equity and bond markets.
But Richard Burton at Cavill White Securities said the market was falling away on local influences, namely a series of poorly-received results as the reporting season progresses.
"Telecom being re-rated downward has created a big sell-off," Burton said.
Wall Street had had some effect on local sentiment.
"But Telecom was down 25 cents in the States and that was really what spooked this market. Plus we've had a series of poor results," he said.
On that score, Fletcher Paper ended even at NZ$2.90 after earlier dipping to $2.85 following Wednesday's divisional results for the first half.
FCL Energy, which reported by far the strongest outcome from all the divisions, dropped six to NZ$3.76.
Fletcher Building dropped two to NZ$4.31 and FCL Forests lost five to $2.08.
Analysts said Wednesday's first half results represented a mixed bag for the Fletcher group.
Brierley Investments was relatively steady at NZ$1.38, down two, while Lion Nathan posted a modest five-cent rebound to $3.54.
Outside the top five, The New Zealand Refining Co firmed 25 cents after reporting a lift in operating earnings while Tranz Rail dropped by the same amount to NZ$8.40.
Tranz Rail has a stock overhang now that Berkshire Fund has signalled its intention to sell 9.84 million Tranz Rail shares.
